findings.text: The Goal and Rationale of the feature baseline.run still say that the baseline commands change nothing but the manifest and the coherence file, and call that the capability's invariant. baseline.run.writes now also lets manifest remove the amendment note.

No rule covers a spec root whose amendment_note exists but cannot be read, or is not UTF-8 as system.amendment-note requires. baseline.pack.note only separates a note holding more than whitespace from one that does not, so neither its Then nor its Otherwise covers this case, and neither does pack.exit-status 2.

system.amendment-note says the note holds no headings, but nothing checks this: lint skips the file, and pack copies it as the file holds it. A note that holds a level-1 heading would break pack_text's five-heading structure, and no rule says what happens then.

The row 'a folder named `.amendment.md`' of baseline.pack.note-unreadable calls a folder an `amendment_note`, but system.amendment-note defines it as the file `.amendment.md`. If a folder is no amendment_note, baseline.pack.note's Otherwise applies (nothing taken, everything else as it was, so pack goes on and exits 0), which contradicts that row's exit status 2.

`system.amendment-note` now counts anything named `.amendment.md` as the note, whatever it is, and says `manifest` removes it. But `baseline.manifest.write` only covers whether `manifest_file` can be written. No rule says what `manifest` does when the note is a folder (removed with its contents, or not), or when the note cannot be removed: its Then still promises exit status 0 with the note removed.

baseline.manifest.remove makes `manifest` exit with 2 after `manifest_file` was written, when an entry cannot be removed, and exit with 0 only once every entry is removed. But `manifest.exit-status` still defines 0 as "the manifest was written" and 2 as "the manifest could not be written, or the command could not run". A written manifest with a failed removal fits neither definition, and the written manifest alone no longer earns 0.

The Otherwise of baseline.manifest.remove names only the entries that could not be removed. It does not say what happens to the others: when `.amendment.md` can be removed and `.coherence.json` cannot, no rule says whether `.amendment.md` is removed or stays. The Examples have no such row.

The Rationale of baseline.manifest.remove says whatever stands under the coherence file's name is removed, and a folder goes with everything in it. But `coherence_file` is defined as "the file `.coherence.json`", unlike `amendment_note`, which is "the entry, whatever it is". And baseline.run.writes exempts `.amendment.md` "with everything in it" but only `.coherence.json` itself. So removing a folder named `.coherence.json` with its contents would break the invariant, while reading the definition literally means such a folder is not the coherence file and is not removed.
